summary: The root عفر (Efr) primarily describes something wicked, malignant, or cunning, often exceeding ordinary bounds.
lane: عِفْرٌ ذ A boar; (S, O, K;) as also : or a swine, as a common term: or the young one of a sow. (K.) -A2- عِفْرٌ (S, A, O, K) and (Sgh in TA in art. نفر ) and , (A, O, K,) in which the ى is to render the word quasi-coordinate to شِرْذِمَةٌ , [I substitute this word for شِرْذِوَةٌ , in the L, and شِرْذِذَةٌ in the TA,] and the ة to give intensiveness, (L, TA,) and , (A, O, K,) in which the ت is to render the word quasicoordinate to قِنْدِيلٌ , (TA,) [or to render it a contraction of عِفْرِيَةٌ ,] and , which occurs in one reading of the Kur, [xxvii. 39, and is agreeable with modern vulgar pronunciation,] (O, CK,) and , (CK,) and , (A, O, L, K,) in which the ى is to render the word quasi-coordinate to عُذَافِرَةٌ , and the ة is to give intensiveness, (TA,) and , (O, K,) and , (Sgh, K,) and , (Sgh, K,) and , and , (Lh, TA,) and , (Lth, TA,) [respecting which last, see the latter portion of this paragraph,] applied to a man, (S, O, K,) and to a jinnee, or genie, (Kur, ubi suprá,) Wicked, or malignant; (S, O, K;) crafty, or cunning; (S, O;) abominable, foul, or evil; (K;) abounding in evil; (TA;) strong, or powerful; (A;) insolent and audacious in pride and in acts of rebellion or disobedience; (A, TA;) who roils his adversary in the dust: (A:) and the epithet applied to a woman is عِفْرَةٌ , (S, O,) and , (Lh, K,) and : (Sh, O:) or signifies anything that exceeds the ordinary bounds; and is syn. with it: (AO, S, O:) and and and (Zj, K) applied to a man, and as applied in the Kur, ubi suprá, [to a jinnee,] (Zj,) sharp, vigorous, and effective, in an affair, exceeding the ordinary bounds therein, with craftiness, or cunning, (Zj, O, K,) and wickedness, or malignity: (Zj:) or is properly applied to a jinnee, and signifies evil in disposition, and wicked or malignant; and is metaphorically applied to a man, like as is شَيْطَانٌ : (B:) it is applied to an evil jinnee that is powerful, but inferior to such as is termed مَارِدٌ : (Mir-át ez-Zemán:) also signifies i. q. دَاهِيَةٌ [app. meaning very crafty or cunning, rather than a calamity ]: (S, O:) and are also applied as epithets to a شَيْطَان [or devil]: (Kh, S:) the pl. of the former of these two epithets is عَفَارِيَةٌ , (Kh, S, O,) or عَفَارِىُّ ; (Fr;) and that of is عَفَارِيتُ ; (Kh, Fr, S, O;) and that of is عِفِرُّونَ ; (Sh;) and that of عِفْرٌ is أَعْفَارٌ . (TA in art. جشم .) You say, فُلَانٌ نِفْرِيتٌ , and نِفْرِيَةٌ ; [ Such a one is wicked, or malignant; &c.;] the latter of these two words being an imitative sequent. (AO, S, O.) And in a trad. it is said, إِنَّ ٱللّٰهَ يَبْغُضُ النِّفْرِيَةَ ٱلَّذِى لَا يُرْزَأُ فِى أَهْلٍ وَلَامَالٍ (AO, S) [ Verily God hates ] the crafty or cunning, the wicked or malignant, the abounding in evil; or him who collects much and refuses to give; or him who acts very wrongfully or unjustly or tyrannically; [ who will not suffer loss in his family nor in his property. ] (TA.) -b2- أَسَدٌ عِفْرٌ , and , and , and , (K,) and , (TA,) and , (K, [respecting which see what follows: in the CK عَفَرْتٰى , which is wrong in two respects:]) A strong, (K,) powerful, great, (TA,) lion: (K, TA:) or العَفَرْنَى the lion; so called because of his strength: (S, O:) and لَبُؤَةٌ عَفَرْنًى , (S, O, TA,) like the masc., (TA. [or it may be in this case with the fem. ى , i. e. without tenween,]) or , (K, TA,) a strong lioness: (S, O, K:) or the epithet, of either gender, signifies bold: from عَفَرٌ signifying “ dust, ” or from عَفْرٌ in the sense of اِعْتِفَارٌ , or from the strength and hardiness of the animal: (TA:) and نَاقَةٌ عَفَرْنَاةٌ a strong she-camel; pl. عَفَرْنَيَاتٌ : (S, O:) but you do not say جَمَلٌ عَفَرْنًى ; (Az:) the alif [which is in this case written ى ] and ن in عَفَرْنًى are to render it quasi-coordinate to سَفَرْجَلٌ [which shows that it is with tenween]. (S.)

headwords.def: aor. عَفِرَ, (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. عَفْرٌ, (S, O, Msb,) He rubbed it (namely a vessel) with dust: and he rubbed it much with dust: (Msb:) or the latter, he defiled, or soiled, it with dust: (Mgh:) and the former, and ↓ latter, (S, O, K,) of which the inf. n. is تَعْفِيرٌ, (S, O,) he rolled, or turned over, him, or it, فِى التُّرَابِ in the dust: (S, O, K:) or he hid ( دَسَّ ) him, or it, therein. (K.) It is is said in a trad.

عَفَّرَ see 1, in four places. عفّر قِرْنَهُ, and فَأَلْزَقَهُ بِالعَفَرِ, He wrestled with his adversary, and made him cleave to the dust. (A.) عفّر, inf. n. تَعْفِيرٌ, He mixed his black sheep or goats with others of the colour termed عُفْرَةٌ: (O, K, TA:) or he took white sheep or goats in exchange for black; because the former have more increase. (S, O, TA.) And He made, or rendered, white. (S, O.)
عَاْفَرَ see the next preceding paragraph.
تَعَفَّرَ see 7, in three places. تعفّر الوَحْشُ (tropical:) The wild animals became fat. (O, K, TA.)
said of [food of the kind called] ثَرِيد, It was made white. (K. [See أَعْفَرُ, latter half.])

and It (a vessel) became rubbed with dust: and it became much rubbed with dust: (Msb:) or the first and ↓ second, (S, O,) and ↓ the last also, (O,) it (a thing) became defiled with dust: (S, O:) or the first and ↓ last, he or it, became rolled, or turned over, فِى التُّرَابِ in the dust: or became hidden therein. (K.) And one says, دَخَلْتُ المَآءَ فَمَا ٱنْعَفَرَتْ قَدَمَاىَ I entered the water, and my feet did not reach the ground. (A, TA.)
إِعْتَفَرَ see 1, in four places. See also 7, in two places.

Q. Q. 2 تَعَفْرَتَ He became, or acted like, an عِفْرِيت; (K, TA;) from which latter word this verb is derived, the [final] augmentative letter being preserved in it, with the radical letters, to convey the full meaning, and to indicate the original. (TA.)
: see عَفَرٌ, in four places.
: see عِفْرٌ. Also pl. of أَعْفَرُ [q. v.]. (S, &c.)

A boar; (S, O, K;) as also: or a swine, as a common term: or the young one of a sow. (K.) عِفْرٌ (S, A, O, K) and (Sgh in TA in art. نفر ) and, (A, O, K,) in which the ى is to render the word quasi-coordinate to شِرْ ِمَةٌ, [I substitute this word for شِرْ ِوَةٌ, in the L, and شِرْ ِ َةٌ in the TA,] and the ة to give intensiveness, (L, TA,) and, (A, O, K,) in which the ت is to render the word quasicoordinate to قِنْدِيلٌ, (TA,) [or to render it a contraction of عِفْرِيَةٌ,] and, which…

(IDrd, S, A, O, Msb, K) and (IDrd, A, O, K) Dust: (IDrd, S, O, Msb:) [like عَفَارٌ the dust of the earth: (Freytag, from Meyd:)] or the exterior of the dust or earth: (A, K:) and the surface of the earth; (Msb;) as also الأَرْضِ: (TA:) pl. أَعْفَارٌ. (K.) You say مَا عَلَى الأَرْضِ مِثْلُهُ There is not upon the face of the earth the like of him, or it.
[part. n. of عَفِرَ ]. أَرْضٌ عَفِرَةٌ Land of the colour termed عُفْرَةٌ [q. v.]. (O and TA in art. عثر.) See also عِفْرٌ.
and the fem., with ة: see عِفْرٌ, in four places.

A dust-colour inclining to whiteness; a whitish dust-colour: (TA:) or whiteness that is not clear: (Mgh, Msb:) or whiteness that is not very clear, (AZ, As,) like the colour of the surface of the earth: (AZ, As, Mgh:) or whiteness with a tinge of redness over it: (A:) the colour of an antelope such as is termed أَعْفَرُ. (K.) See also عِفْرِيَةٌ, in three places.
or عَفْرًى: see عِفْرِيَةٌ.
: see عِفْرٌ, first quarter.
: see عِفْرِيَةٌ.
: see عِفْرٌ, first quarter: and see the next paragraph, in three places.

: see عِفْرٌ, in six places. The hair, and the feathers, of the back of the neck, of the lion, and of the cock, &c., which it turns back towards the top of its head when exasperated; as also (S, O) and, (S,) or: (O, TA:) and, the feathers around the neck of a cock and of a bustard ( حُبَارَى ) &c.: (S in art.
; and عَفْرِيتٌ: and the fem., عِفْرِيتَةٌ: see عِفْرٌ, in ten places.
: see عِفْرٌ, in two places.

: see عِفْرٌ, in two places. لَيْثُ عِفِرِّينَ The lion. (AA, K.) So in the prov., إِنَّهُ لَأَشْجَعُ مِنْ لَيْثِ عِفِرِّينَ [ Verily he is more courageous than the lion ]. (AA, TA.) عِفِرِّينُ is the name of a certain place in which are lions, or abounding with lions: (S, O, K:) or the name of a certain country or town.
and عَفَرْنَاةٌ: see عِفْرٌ, in three places. The latter also signifies The [ kind of goblin, or demon, called ] غُولٌ. (O, K.)
: see عِفْرٌ; first quarter. and see عِفْرِيَةٌ.

: see عَفَرٌ. Also A certain kind of tree, (S, O, K,) by means of which fire is produced; (S, O;) زِنَاد [or pieces of wood, or stick, used for that purpose, ] being made of its branches: (K, * TA:) accord.
The quality, or disposition, of him who is termed عِفْرٌ and عِفْرِيَةٌ and عِفْرِيتٌ &c.; i. e., wickedness, or malignity, &c. (K, * TA.)
: see عِفْرٌ, in three places.
and and and Defiled with dust: hence, العَافِرُ الوَجْهِ He whose face is defiled with dust: and هُوَ الوَجْهِ فِى التُّرَابِ, and, He has the face defiled in the dust. (TA.)

وَقَعُوا فِى عَافُورِ شَرٍّ , (S, K,) and فِى شَرٍّ, (TA,) i. q. فِى عَاثُورِ شَرٍّ, (Fr, S, K,) i. e., They fell into difficulty, or distress. (S.) Some say that the ف is substituted for ث. (TA.) [But see عاثور.]

Dust-coloured inclining to white; of a whitish dust-colour: (TA:) or white, but not of a clear hue: (Msb:) or, applied to a buckantelope, white, but not of a very clear white, (AZ, As, S, O, K,) being like the colour of the surface of the earth: (AZ, As, Mgh:) or a buck-antelope having a tinge of red over his whiteness, (AA, S, A, K,) with a short neck; and such is the weakest of antelopes in running: (AA, S, O:) or having a redness in his back, with white flanks: (K:) [in the CK,…
: see عَافِرٌ, in two places.

One whose sheep or goats are of the colour termed عُفْرَةٌ: there is no tribe among the Arabs to whom this appellation applies, except Hudheyl. (A, TA.) [Accord. to analogy, this should rather be written مُعْفِرٌ; and perhaps it is thus in correct copies of the A.]
: see عَافِرٌ. أَرْضٌ مَعْفُورَةٌ Land of which the herbage has been eaten. (S, O.)
: see مَعَافِرِىٌّ, in three places.
(tropical:) One who walks with companies of travellers, (S, O, K, TA,) and so, accord. to the L,, (TA,) and obtains of their superabundance [ of provisions ]. (S, O, TA.)

ثَوْبٌ مَعَافِرِىٌّ , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) pl. ثِيَابٌ مَعَافِرِيَّةٌ, (S, O, K,) and بُرْدٌ مَعَافِرِىٌّ, (Az,) and hence, simply,, (Az, Mgh,) as a subst., (Az,) without the relative ى, (Az, Mgh,) accord. to As, (Mgh,) A kind of garment, or piece of cloth, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and a garment of the kind called بُرْد, (Az,) so called in relation to, (S, O, K, &c.,) a word imperf. decl., (S, O, K,) because of its being of the form of an imperf. decl.
: see مُعَافِرٌ.
: see عَافِرٌ, in two places.

The dust-coloured gazelle: (K:) or the gazelle, as a general term: (K, * TA:) as also يُعْفُورٌ: (K:) and the [ young gazelle such as is called ] خِشْف: (S, O, K:) or the buck-gazelle: (S, Mgh, O:) and (S, IAth, O, in the Mgh “ or ”) the young one of the wild cow: (S, IAth, Mgh, O:) n. un. with ة: (TA:) pl. يَعَافِيرُ. (S, O.) Also A light, or an active, ass.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
